clue.text: Secure worker initiating strike

indicators.note: the worker comes first, starting off the word that follows it

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a farmhand
to cuff is to strike with the open hand

explanation.surface: A labourer is the one who sets a walkout going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initiating' says the worker starts the word; 'strike' looks like industrial action alongside 'worker', but it means a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure a prisoner is to restrain the wrists with linked metal rings.

clue.text: Pull up after reptile is seen on the road

indicators.note: the pull-up comes after the reptile in the word

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
to pull up is to halt, to come to a stop

explanation.surface: A driver stops behind a snake lying on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets the halt behind the snake. The definition is descriptive: the material is what you see laid on a road surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the tarry paving material that surfaces roads.

clue.text: Discount for the long suit of Holmes

explanation.surface: A price reduction is the strength of the great detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long suit' means a strong point, as in card games, not clothing; Sherlock Holmes's great skill was reasoning things out.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction in price is a deduction; and logical inference from clues was the detective's speciality.

clue.text: Wind away in a French dance

parts.note: un is the French for a
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: Something winds its way through a dance from France.
explanation.definitionFit: To unreel is to unwind something from a spool, letting it out.

clue.text: Daring stuff — case for revising the details

indicators.note: revising the letters means reworking them into a new order

explanation.surface: Bold material in a legal case needs its particulars revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revising' signals the anagram of DARING STUFF CASE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures are the hard data, the particulars of a matter.

clue.text: Birds of varied shape

explanation.surface: Birds come in many forms.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the old adjective, meaning various or sundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Loons and grebes that plunge under water are so named; the archaic adjective means sundry or several kinds.

clue.text: Disadvantage for a ward?

parts.note: the reading tells you to take the word draw and turn it round, which spells the word ward

explanation.surface: Is there a downside for someone in guardianship?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, makes the clue word, since DRAW written backwards is WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a snag or handicap that counts against something.

clue.text: What am I up to? Stop, start veto.

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: asked what am I, the speaker answers me
to bar is to stop or block
go is a start, as in having a go

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what's happening, then halts plans and starts a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ME into EM, followed by BAR and GO.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, a prohibition on trade or publication.

clue.text: Solo entertainment or diversion in a decent spa

indicators.note: a diversion sends things off course, here the letters of the words decent spa

explanation.surface: A one-person show or other amusement is staged at a respectable resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' looks like part of the definition next to 'entertainment', but it is the anagram signal; 'or' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A step dance is performed by one dancer, an individual display of fancy footwork.

clue.text: Silk producer seen in conversation with the king

indicators.note: words said in conversation are spoken, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: seen in the sense of spotted, spied
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A silk maker is spotted chatting with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conversation' makes SPIED heard, which spelt another way is SPIDE; R then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders spin silk thread to build webs.

clue.text: Head of church owns off-blue vestment

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to own is to have, so owns gives has

indicators.note: off means the letters of blue are out of order

explanation.surface: A senior cleric has a faded blue robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-blue' looks like a colour, but 'off' signals the anagram of BLUE (BULE).
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is the sleeveless outer robe worn by a priest celebrating Mass.

clue.text: Bags that go with shining morning faces

definitions.text: Bags that go with shining morning faces

parts.words: Bags that go with shining morning faces
parts.note: an allusion to Shakespeare's seven ages of man in As You Like It: the whining schoolboy carries his school bag, with shining morning face

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Jaques's 'All the world's a stage' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: These are schoolchildren's shoulder bags, carried by the schoolboy in the famous speech.

clue.text: Stopped by something like a gate

explanation.surface: Something resembling a gate halted progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by something' is link padding; the second sense is fitted with bars, as a gate is.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopped means blocked or prohibited; a gate is made of crosswise rails, so it is striped with them.

clue.text: Having to speak, remained sober

indicators.note: having to speak means the word is said, so its sound counts, not its spelling

parts.note: remained means stayed

explanation.surface: Called on to make a speech, someone kept a straight face.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid means sedate and serious, sober in manner.

clue.text: Note to block a humorous epithet

parts.note: so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
a briquet, also spelt briquette, is a small block of compressed coal dust

explanation.surface: A memo is used to obstruct a funny label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'block' looks like a verb with 'to'; it is a noun for BRIQUET, a compressed coal block.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is a nickname, often a jokey one.

clue.text: Very low price for being put on canvas

explanation.surface: A bargain price for a portrait being painted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on canvas' suggests painting, but the canvas is a boxing ring's floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock-bottom price is a knockdown one; a boxer floored by a blow is sent to the mat.

clue.text: Character of tragedy unusually so amended

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an unusual way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A tragic role has been rewritten in an odd way.
explanation.definitionFit: Desdemona is Othello's wife in Shakespeare's tragedy, murdered by her jealous husband.

clue.text: English policeman is noteworthy

parts.note: a special is a special constable, a volunteer part-time police officer in Britain

explanation.surface: An English police officer is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: A special constable is a British volunteer police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial means exceptional, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Succeeds as Grace Darling does

explanation.surface: Someone does well, like a famous heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling, a lighthouse keeper's daughter, rowed out in 1838 to rescue survivors from a wrecked steamer off the Northumberland coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull off a feat is to manage it; to rescue people from a wreck is to get them away to safety.

clue.text: Drives in spectacles, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word sounds like another

parts.note: spectacles in the sense of sights, things to see

explanation.surface: A motorist motors about wearing glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' suggests glasses, but it means sights; heard, they become CITES.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to urge on or push someone into action.

clue.text: In the end you get wise to this habit

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: sage means wise

explanation.surface: Eventually you'll learn to know this custom well.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the way things are habitually done.

clue.text: Giant oil rig sited in old city

indicators.note: sited in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the old city

parts.note: Gath was an ancient Philistine city

indicators.note: to rig is to fix or fiddle, so the letters of oil are rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge oil platform stands in an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rig' looks like the drilling platform but is the anagram signal, and 'sited in' is the container; Gath was the giant's home town in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the giant Philistine from Gath killed by David.

clue.text: Harmony for a short time in wedlock

indicators.note: in places the short time inside the word for wedlock

parts.note: a union is a marriage
s is the abbreviation for a second, a short time

explanation.surface: Married bliss lasts only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing in unison means all on the same note, in agreement.

clue.text: Entrance money?

parts.note: read as two words, the earnings are what comes in, the money that enters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance money' suggests an admission fee; it is money coming in.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is the money one receives, money that arrives in one's account.

clue.text: Guardedly drink with German lady avoiding publicity

parts.note: gin is a spirit

indicators.note: avoiding means the word lady goes without the publicity

parts.note: ad, short for advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: Cautiously, a German woman drinks while shunning the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes AD from LADY to leave LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingerly means cautiously, with great care.

clue.text: Hidden in the future

explanation.surface: Concealed in times to come.
explanation.walkthrough: The rarer second sense is later or further on, from Latin for further.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulterior motive is concealed; the word also means coming later, subsequent.

clue.text: Motto representing goal in partnership

indicators.note: in places the reordered letters inside the partnership

parts.note: in bridge, North and South form a partnership

indicators.note: representing as in re-presenting, putting the letters forward in a new order

explanation.surface: A catchphrase standing for the aim of a business partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representing' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container; bridge players sit as two partnerships, North-South and East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a catchy motto or phrase used in advertising or politics.

clue.text: Clothing quotas seldom include, decorative cords

indicators.note: the words quotas seldom include the answer within them, across the word break

explanation.surface: Fashion allowances rarely cover ornamental trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' is surface padding pointing to the garment trim; the answer is singular against 'cords', as a tassel is a bunch of cords.
explanation.definitionFit: A tassel is a tuft of loose threads or cords bound at one end as ornament.

clue.text: Lie in a hot spot for appearance sake

definitions.text: Lie in a hot spot for appearance sake

parts.words: Lie in a hot spot for appearance sake
parts.note: lying in the heat for the sake of looks suggests a tan, not a hiding place or a dangerous place

explanation.walkthrough: 'hot spot' suggests trouble or a nightclub; it is literally a sunny place.
explanation.definitionFit: To bask in sunshine to get a tan is to expose the skin to the rays.
